basis: Defining hair/skin/nail disorder; developmental disability/ataxia, brachydactyly/hypermobility and dental malocclusion each reported in 1/1; population frequencies uncertain.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: structural dental malocclusion affects the oral axis in 1/1 reported patient; evidence is limited.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental disability, ataxia and reduced reflexes occurred in 1/1; these are associated manifestations rather than the defining hair defect.

basis: Hereditary motor neuropathy; persistent distal muscle wasting in 3/3 represents muscle tissue loss; structural pes cavus in 1/3 also supports musculoskeletal involvement.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: distal muscle atrophy in 3/3 is persistent tissue loss despite its neurogenic origin; pes cavus is reported in 1/3 (~33%).

basis: Tooth grinding and oral clenching define bruxism; teeth map to gastrointestinal. Muscle overactivity alone does not establish muscle or joint damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: jaw clenching alone establishes neither muscle disease nor joint injury; temporomandibular disorders are separate diagnoses.

basis: Asphyxiating skeletal dysplasia with defining respiratory failure (80-99%); renal malformations and hepatic fibrosis each 30-79%. Cardiovascular anomalies (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: respiratory failure is a defining feature of asphyxiating thoracic dysplasia, with insufficiency reported in 80-99%.

basis: Cleft lip/palate is a structural defect of the mouth. No additional generalized skeletal disease is established by the facial-skeleton ancestor.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: oral clefting maps to the mouth; the facial-skeleton ancestor does not establish an additional musculoskeletal manifestation.

basis: Microcephalic primordial skeletal dwarfism; microphthalmia and microdontia/microglossia each reported in 1/1 assessed patient. Small samples limit certainty; renal ectopia is <30%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: microdontia and microglossia are intrinsic structural oral abnormalities, each reported in 1/1 assessed patient; frequency estimates are fragile.

basis: Usual optic neuritis is immune-mediated optic-nerve inflammation; toxic/nutritional forms are minority exceptions. The optic nerve maps to ocular; associated MS is separate.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: most usual optic neuritis is immune-mediated demyelinating inflammation; the broader umbrella's toxic/nutritional exceptions do not dominate.

basis: ABCD1 metabolic disease presents with adrenal failure; neurologic disability usually (>50%) develops by middle age as part of the same disease's natural history.

decisions.neurologic: involved: the definition explicitly states neurologic disability usually (>50%) develops by middle age; this is evolution of ABCD1 disease, not a separate coincidental disorder.

basis: Ataxia, amyotrophy and deafness define the syndrome (80-99% each); delayed puberty/testicular abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Pigment patches (30-79%) lack demonstrated functional skin damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: hypopigmented patches occur in 30-79%, but pigment change alone does not demonstrate skin injury or loss of function.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: amyotrophy is a defining component of the named syndrome, with skeletal muscle atrophy in 80-99%; persistent tissue loss qualifies despite neurogenic origin.

basis: Hereditary motor-pathway degeneration; skeletal muscle atrophy in 3/3 assessed patients is persistent muscle tissue loss. Contractures and scoliosis are only occasional (<30%).

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: skeletal muscle atrophy in 3/3 assessed patients documents common persistent tissue loss; neurogenic origin does not negate it. Contractures/scoliosis alone are <30%.
